title: Japan's mission to a moon of Mars
credits: Photos: SpaceX, NASA / Unsplash · Map: Natural Earth
lines: Japan has launched one of the boldest missions in space exploration.
On October nineteenth, an H3 rocket lifted off from the Tanegashima Space Center, carrying a spacecraft called M M X.
It is led by Japan's space agency, JAXA, with help from NASA and the European Space Agency.
Its target is Phobos, the larger of the two small moons that circle Mars.
After about ten months in space, it should reach Mars in August, twenty twenty-seven.
There, it will map Phobos, choose landing sites, and touch down twice to collect samples.
A small French and German rover, called IDEFIX, is also due to drive on its surface.
The goal is to bring back about ten grams of Phobos soil.
The spacecraft is set to leave Mars in November, twenty thirty.
And its sample capsule should land in Australia, in twenty thirty-one.
If it succeeds, it will be the first sample ever brought back from the Mars system.
